findings.description: `RegisteredProject` (interface, lines 12-25) and `FleetBlock` (type, lines 31-38) are exported directly from `fleet.service.ts`, a `.service.ts` file, instead of living in `src/core/types/`.
findings.body:
`docs/conventions/general.md` (lines 64-69): "Exported types live in `*.types.ts` under the area's `types/` folder — `src/core/types/`, `src/adapters/types/`. **Never inline an exported `type`/`interface` in a `*.service.ts` or `*.routes.ts` file** — the spot-check hook warns on this. Re-export from the consumer if you want a stable call-site path."

`src/core/fleet.service.ts` exports `RegisteredProject` and `FleetBlock` directly from this new service file rather than from `src/core/types/`. `docs/09-decisions.md` decision 65 explains the placement choice ("owned by core and exported from `fleet.service.ts`, the reader that consumes it"), but decision 65's precedence clause only overrides docs/00–08, not `docs/conventions/*`, so it doesn't excuse this. `src/core/types/` already exists with 12 files, and `fleet.service.ts` already imports from `./types/dashboard.types.js`, so moving these two types there (and re-exporting to `project.utils.ts`/`dashboard-text.utils.ts` as needed) is a small, mechanical move.

findings.description: `listProjects<T extends { id: string; repoPath: string }>(...)` uses a bare `T` generic parameter, which the naming convention forbids.
findings.body:
`docs/conventions/general.md` line 86: "**Generics are descriptive** — `TConfig`, `TResponse`. Never bare `T` / `U`."

`listProjects` in `src/core/project.service.ts:21` uses a bare `T`. Two pre-existing files (`src/core/report-data.utils.ts:6`, `src/cli/no-adapter-guard.utils.ts:4`) already do this, but they predate this PR and the rule's "Never" wording doesn't grandfather new code repeating it. Biome's configured preset (`recommended`) doesn't include `useNamingConvention`, so `LINT_CMD` won't catch this — it's a genuine gap only a convention-aware reviewer catches.

findings.description: `fleet.service.ts`'s new `FleetStore`/`FleetReading` interfaces are hand-maintained structural duplicates of `ActionDeps`/`DashboardReading` in `src/cli/ui/actions.service.ts` and `use-snapshot.hook.ts`, which `AppProps.read` actually expects — they compile today only via structural typing, so a future field rename on either side won't propagate to the other; a shared `*.types.ts` importable from both `src/cli/ui` and `src/core` would remove the hand-sync burden.

`fleetLines`/`fleetBlockLines`, newly added here, assemble a whole multi-project report (separators, pluralized hidden-count line, refusal-vs-snapshot branching) from a core-service-shaped `FleetBlock[]`, a different responsibility level than this file's other nine single-session label exports; the file's own header comment ("Nothing here decides anything") no longer holds for these two functions, which are the only exports here consumed solely by `index.ts` and the only ones importing a core-service type.

The JSDoc above `canonicalPath` ("Where `path` resolves to on disk, or undefined when nothing is there.") paraphrases the signature rather than giving a WHY — no invariant or gotcha about why a thrown `realpathSync` should be treated as "nothing," unlike the neighboring `RegisteredProject.repoExists` doc which does explain that.

Decision 65's caveat paragraph is labeled "**The ceiling.**" (bold, singular), breaking this file's own established convention of "*Ceilings.*" (italic, plural) used consistently in all 10 other instances in this file — a reader scanning for the recurring marker won't recognize this one as the same kind of section.

The clause appended to the intro paragraph — "...is refused as `not its own path: a variant of a repo path, never opened` — the fleet views' refusal, on `--project <id>` too (decision 65)." — tacks "on `--project <id>` too (decision 65)" onto an em-dash appositive with no governing verb, reading as a dangling fragment; something like "— the fleet views' refusal since decision 61, now firing on `--project <id>` too (decision 65)" would state plainly that the refusal now also covers `--project <id>`.

The `pup project list` bullet documenting the line format (`<id>  <repo_path>  active|dormant since <when>  conductor running|stopped`, with `(missing)` when the repo is gone) wasn't updated to mention the new `(not its own path)` suffix this PR adds to `registryLine`'s output, leaving the CLI reference silent about a marker this exact PR introduces.

The "named, not counted, like the brief's list..." rationale, which in `index.ts` sat as an inline comment directly above the `const live = [...]` array it explains, is now folded into `putProjectToSleep`'s top-of-function JSDoc; the reader hits this explanation before two unrelated early-return branches and has to carry it forward several lines to the `live` array it actually justifies.
